core_obligations: Five ports opened; cession of Hong Kong; indemnity; tariff schedule and transit rules
termination_or_breach: Regime altered through later treaties and conflict; not a single short-term concession
quantified_effect: 21 million silver dollars indemnity; treaty specified instalments 1843–1845

article_type: Fixed import tariff and consular jurisdiction

termination_or_breach: Siam renegotiated treaty relations in later decades; jurisdictional privileges ended through later legal reforms
quantified_effect: 3% import duty; opium import duty-free but sale confined to opium farmer/agents

article_type: Unequal treaty, extraterritoriality and tariff autonomy
example: Treaty of Amity and Commerce (Harris Treaty)
parties: Japan; United States (followed by treaties with other powers)
term_or_duration: Effective 1859; revised regime of treaty ports and consular jurisdiction; extraterritoriality ended 1899 after treaty revision
core_obligations: Port opening; tariff schedule; most-favoured-nation treatment; foreign consular jurisdiction
termination_or_breach: Tariff autonomy progressively revised; new treaties took effect 1899, ending extraterritoriality
quantified_effect: 1866 tariff convention imposed uniform 5% ad valorem duties; not a measured GDP loss
source: Japan Customs, History of Japan Customs; Japan MOFA treaty documents

parties: Egypt; Universal Company of the Suez Maritime Canal
term_or_duration: 99 years from canal opening; opened 1869, scheduled expiry 1968
core_obligations: Company receives canal construction/operation concession; Egyptian government appoints director; equal non-discriminatory passage; government receives share of net profits
termination_or_breach: Nationalized by Egypt in 1956, before concession expiry; treaty/concession dispute followed
quantified_effect: Egypt entitled to 15% of annual net profits under concession; contractual entitlement, not realized return
source: Suez Canal Authority history; US FRUS 1955–57 vol.16 doc.1

article_type: Freedom of trade and navigation / transit rights
parties: 14 signatory powers incl. UK, France, Germany, Portugal, Belgium, US
term_or_duration: International act with continuing obligations; later practice and decolonization transformed the regime
core_obligations: Free trade in Congo basin; equal navigation on Congo and Niger; prohibition of exclusive navigation privileges; limits on transit tolls
termination_or_breach: Superseded in practice by colonial partition and later international legal regimes; provisions must be read in historical context
quantified_effect: No transit dues for goods on Congo river under Article 14, except service-equivalent charges
source: German Federal Foreign Office; World and Japan primary text of General Act

example: Meiji government foreign expert contracts (oyatoi gaikokujin)
parties: Japan; hired foreign experts from Britain and other states
term_or_duration: Individual contracts varied; not one international treaty
core_obligations: Foreign experts advised, trained, designed and supervised rail, telegraph, industrial and educational projects
termination_or_breach: Contracts ended/renewed individually; localization and Japanese technical capacity expanded
quantified_effect: About 500 foreign experts employed by Ministry of Industry in 1872 and 1875–78; costs exceeded 50% of its annual budget in those years (source summary)
source: Oxford University Press, Capitalism and Entrepreneurship in the Meiji Period, Public sector chapter

article_type: Long-term alliance, mutual assistance and credit
term_or_duration: 30 years from entry into force (11 Apr 1950); renewable for further five-year periods unless notice one year before expiry
core_obligations: Mutual assistance in event of renewed Japanese aggression; consultation; economic and cultural cooperation; separate agreements on railway/port restoration and credit
termination_or_breach: Treaty later terminated/replaced through 1979 agreement; ideological split undermined cooperation before formal end
quantified_effect: US$300 million credit over five years at 1% annual interest; Chinese Changchun Railway/Port Arthur/Dairen restoration arrangements
source: UN Treaty Series; US FRUS 1950 vol.VI doc.157; World and Japan treaty text
